guidance: Exact document requirements may vary depending on the applicable scheme, state rules, or insurer. Having essential agricultural, identity, and banking records organized in advance helps facilitate verification during survey and claim processing.
information_to_collect: Farmer identity proof (Aadhaar card or other government-approved photo ID)
Bank account details (account number, IFSC code, linked with Aadhaar/DBT)
Land ownership or tenancy proof (Pattadar Passbook, Record of Rights / RoR, or registered tenancy agreement)
Crop sowing details or village revenue certificate (Khasra / Girdawari entry)
Insurance premium deduction receipt, cover note, or bank statement entry
useful_evidence: Clear copies of land records showing survey numbers matching the damaged plot
Bank passbook front page copy showing clear IFSC and account holder name
Official sowing certificate issued by the village revenue officer or agriculture department, if requested
SMS or digital receipt confirming enrollment in the crop insurance scheme
general_next_steps: Ensure digital and physical copies of your identity, land, and bank documents are kept in a safe and accessible place
Verify that your active phone number is correctly linked with your bank account and Aadhaar
Confirm that the insured crop name and surveyed area match your actual cultivation on the ground

guidance: High-quality visual evidence assists surveyors and agricultural committees in verifying the extent, nature, and timing of crop loss. Providing clear, geo-tagged photographs helps prevent ambiguity during official loss assessment.
information_to_collect: Date, time, and exact field location coordinates when photographs are captured
Survey number or recognized plot boundary markers visible in or near the frame
Proportion of the entire field parcel captured across the series of photos
useful_evidence: Geo-tagged and timestamped photographs taken using a mobile device with GPS location enabled
Panoramic wide-angle view establishing field boundaries, access paths, and nearby fixed landmarks (well, pole, road)
Medium shots showing the transition between damaged and less-damaged sections
Close-up shots clearly revealing specific injuries (rotted roots, stripped pods, punctured leaves, lodged stems)
general_next_steps: Capture photographs in bright daylight as soon after the damage event as it is safe to do so
Retain original uncompressed photo files with camera metadata on your phone or memory card
Present the complete photographic sequence to the designated surveyor during the physical inspection visit
